chapters.title: Language Modeling Fundamentals

Perplexity as evaluation metric: intuition, limitations, and why it correlates (imperfectly) with downstream performance

chapters.title: The Attention Mechanism
concepts: From RNNs to attention: the information bottleneck that motivated attention
Scaled dot-product attention: Q, K, V matrices, why we scale by sqrt(d_k), softmax as soft dictionary lookup
Attention as weighted value retrieval: the query-key-value analogy and its limits
Computational cost: O(n²d) time and O(n²) memory — why this matters and what it constrains
Multi-head attention: why multiple heads, what different heads learn, head redundancy

chapters.title: The Original Transformer
concepts: Vaswani et al. (2017) deep dive: encoder-decoder architecture, self-attention, cross-attention
The residual stream view: skip connections as the backbone, attention/FFN as read-write operations
Positional encoding (sinusoidal): why position information is needed and this first solution
Layer normalization placement and the feed-forward sub-layer's role
Training innovations: label smoothing, learning rate warmup, dropout — why each was needed
What the original paper got right and what subsequent work changed

chapters.title: Decoder-Only LLMs
concepts: Causal masking: how it enforces autoregressive structure in self-attention
GPT lineage: GPT-1 (transfer learning), GPT-2 (scale as few-shot), GPT-3 (in-context learning emergence)
Why decoder-only won: simpler architecture, better scaling, unified pre-training objective
Encoder-decoder vs decoder-only tradeoffs: when encoder-decoder still wins (translation, summarization with source)
The pre-train then fine-tune paradigm vs the prompt-based paradigm — architectural implications

chapters.title: Tokenization
concepts: Byte Pair Encoding (BPE): algorithm, merge rules, how vocabulary is built from data
WordPiece and SentencePiece: differences from BPE, unigram model alternative

Tokenization failures: digit splitting, multilingual unfairness, the 'SolidGoldMagikarp' phenomenon
Impact on model architecture: embedding table size, sequence length, positional encoding demands

chapters.title: Positional Encoding
concepts: Why position information is needed: attention is permutation-equivariant without it
Sinusoidal encodings: the original approach, theoretical extrapolation properties, practical limits
Learned positional embeddings: flexibility vs generalization, what GPT-2/3 chose and why
Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE): rotation matrices, relative position encoding, how it enables length extrapolation
ALiBi (Attention with Linear Biases): adding linear bias to attention scores, simpler alternative to RoPE
iRoPE (interleaved RoPE): Llama 4's approach — alternating layers with and without positional encoding

chapters.title: Attention Variants
concepts: Multi-Head Attention (MHA): the baseline, parameter count, memory during inference
Multi-Query Attention (MQA): shared K,V across heads — massive KV-cache savings, quality cost
Grouped-Query Attention (GQA): the middle ground, how LLaMA 2 70B validated it
Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA): DeepSeek's low-rank KV compression, 93% cache reduction
Flash Attention: IO-aware exact attention, tiling for SRAM, why it's algorithmic not approximate
Sliding Window Attention: local context windows, how Mistral trades global attention for efficiency

chapters.title: Feed-Forward Networks, Activations, and Width
concepts: FFN as key-value memory: the 'FFN stores factual knowledge' hypothesis and evidence
Activation functions: ReLU → GELU → SwiGLU — what each improves and the parameter cost of gated variants
GLU variants (Shazeer 2020): why gated linear units consistently outperform standard activations
Width vs depth tradeoffs: wider FFN (more memory capacity) vs deeper network (more composition)

chapters.title: Normalization and Residual Connections
concepts: Layer Normalization: what it normalizes, why BatchNorm fails for Transformers

Pre-norm vs post-norm: training stability tradeoff — pre-norm trains easier but may have representational cost
QK-norm: normalizing queries and keys before attention, how it prevents attention logit growth at scale
The residual stream as information highway: why skip connections are critical for gradient flow and deep networks
Initialization strategies: how weight init interacts with norm placement for training stability

chapters.title: Scaling Laws
concepts: Kaplan et al. (2020): power-law relationships between parameters, data, compute, and loss
Chinchilla (Hoffmann et al. 2022): compute-optimal training — data should scale proportionally with parameters
How Chinchilla changed the field: LLaMA as the direct response (more data, smaller model)
Emergent abilities debate: do capabilities appear suddenly at scale, or is it a measurement artifact?
Scaling laws for downstream tasks: does lower loss always mean better capabilities?
Inference-time scaling: when to spend compute at training vs at inference (relevance to reasoning models)

chapters.title: Pre-training
concepts: Data curation: Common Crawl filtering, deduplication, quality classifiers, data mixing ratios
Training stability: loss spikes, learning rate schedules (cosine, WSD), warmup, gradient clipping
Curriculum learning: does training data ordering matter? Evidence for and against
Two-stage pre-training: OLMo 2's approach — web data first, curated data second
Synthetic data for pre-training: Phi's approach, when synthetic data helps vs hurts

chapters.title: Post-training and Alignment
concepts: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT): instruction tuning, chat formatting, data quality vs quantity
RLHF: reward model training, PPO optimization, KL penalty, why it's hard to get right

Constitutional AI: self-critique, principle-based alignment, Anthropic's approach

chapters.title: Distributed Training
concepts: Data parallelism: replicate model, split data — communication cost of gradient all-reduce
Tensor parallelism (Megatron-LM): splitting individual layers across GPUs, intra-layer communication
Pipeline parallelism: splitting layers across GPUs, micro-batching, bubble overhead
ZeRO (Zero Redundancy Optimizer): sharding optimizer states, gradients, and parameters across GPUs
FSDP (Fully Sharded Data Parallel): PyTorch's ZeRO implementation, communication/compute overlap
Expert parallelism for MoE: all-to-all communication pattern, why MoE training is a distributed systems problem

chapters.title: Mixture of Experts

chapters.title: State Space Models and Alternatives to Attention

Mamba: selective state spaces — input-dependent parameters, hardware-aware scan implementation

chapters.title: Long Context
concepts: The length generalization problem: why models trained on short sequences fail on long ones
RoPE scaling methods: Position Interpolation (PI), NTK-aware interpolation, YaRN — tradeoffs and limits
iRoPE: Llama 4's interleaved approach — some layers position-aware, some position-free
Architectural approaches: chunked attention, hierarchical processing, landmark tokens
Retrieval-augmented architectures: RAG as an alternative to long context, when retrieval beats attention

chapters.title: Multimodal Architectures
concepts: Vision Transformer (ViT): patch embedding, why Transformers work for images
Early fusion vs late fusion: combining modalities at input vs at intermediate layers — tradeoffs

SigLIP and contrastive pre-training: aligning vision and language representations
Pan-and-Scan (Gemma 3): decomposing images into multiple views vs resize-and-pad

chapters.title: Case Study: LLaMA 3 and Llama 4

Llama 4 Maverick: 128 experts — what changes when you scale expert count by 8x

chapters.title: Case Study: DeepSeek-V3

chapters.title: Case Study: Jamba

chapters.title: Case Study: Mamba-2

chapters.title: Case Study: Qwen 3

Aggressive MoE sparsity: 30B total, 3B active — extreme ratio of total-to-active parameters

chapters.title: Case Study: OLMo 2
concepts: Fully open: weights, data, training code, intermediate checkpoints, training logs — why this matters for research
QK-norm: normalizing queries and keys before attention — stabilizing training at scale
Two-stage pre-training: stage 1 on web data, stage 2 on curated data — why and how it improves quality
